conviction_note: Nothing company-level and unpriced was found. Peers and macro data for June-August improved, but RGP has diverged from its peers for two years and said North America was flat sequentially. The CFO left five days before the print without a stated reason, and that is public. This name sold its last Q1 beat of every outlook range (-4.0%). So p_up 46 on an abs_move of 9 (median reaction 7.0, raised for the Q2 guide that comes with this print and for thin coverage) gives -0.72, close to the findings' own sum of -0.6.
bar: Company guide for FQ1 FY27 (quarter ended 2026-08-29), given 2026-07-22: revenue $97-102m (midpoint $99.5m), gross margin 37-38%, run-rate SG&A $41-43m, non-run-rate $2-3m. That implies adjusted EBITDA of about -$4 to -5m (https://www.webull.com/news/15273192387929088 ; the guide is confirmed at https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3411615/resources-connection-reports-financial-results-for-fourth-quarter-and-full-fiscal-year-2026). EPS consensus is disputed: -$0.17 (AAII/Zacks, 3 analysts, no revisions in the past month, https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/518544-what-you-need-to-know-about-resources-connection-incs-q1-earnings, 2026-10-07), -$0.22 (Earnings Whispers snippet), Noble -$0.26. No revenue consensus could be sourced, so the revenue bar is the company guide. The stock most likely trades on the FQ2 revenue guide, which has no sourced bar.
positioning_check: Short interest 802,076 shares, 2.45% of float, 2.6 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-15, down 14.5% from the prior report (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/RGP/short-interest/). Not crowded. The option chain is unusable (ATM legs not two-sided, total OI 187, put/call OI 0.01), so there is no skew or implied move. The baseline scale is the 7.0% median historical reaction, with 6 of 8 prints down. Spot $3.725 is 7.35% above the 52-week low and 29.45% below the high; run-up is -3.75% over 20 days and -0.93% over 5. Tieton Capital disclosed 8.2% on a 13G filed 2026-08-12.

findings.finding: The CFO (Jennifer Ryu) resigned effective 2026-10-02, five days before this print, with no reason given. The interim CFO is the Chief AI Officer, Jessica Block (joined March 2026). On 2026-09-17 the board named the corporate controller Chief Accounting Officer effective 2026-10-03, with a guaranteed FY27 target bonus of $150k. This print and the FQ2 guide will be presented by a finance team in place for five days.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior RGP print came under a CFO hand-off this close to the date. The last two leadership transitions (CEO and COO separations in FY26, $12.2m in costs) coincided with the -14.6% (2026-01-07) and -18.4% (2026-07-22) prints, both on revenue and guidance. That is correlation, not this line.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public (8-K, 2026-09-03), so the fact is not hidden. What is unpriced is how a five-day-old interim finance team handles the guide: conservative re-basing, wider ranges or new cost actions. If the market had priced a re-based guide, the stock would have broken the $3.47 52-week low. It sits 7% above it, and short interest fell 14.5% into mid-September.
findings.independence: The CAO 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1084765/000108476526000069/rgp-20260917.htm, 2026-09-21) is the same transition, so it is one finding, not two. The finance chief left with no stated disagreement, and no 8-K mentions a material weakness or a reliance issue.

findings.finding: Staffing demand in the overlapping period improved. Robert Half's F&A contract talent revenue was -1.3% y/y adjusted in CQ2 2026 against -6.3% in CQ1, with a third consecutive quarter of sequential growth in talent solutions and 'hiring demand continues to improve' (reported 2026-07-23, the day after RGP last spoke). BLS temp help employment rose +6,800 in August, an eighth straight monthly gain, +1.5% y/y. RGP's own guide implied about -17% y/y revenue for the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on this line. RGP fell -18.4% on 2026-07-22 even though peer data was already stabilising, so peer improvement has not transmitted to RGP's reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer and macro improvement has not shown up in RGP's price: it trades near the lows, with a -3.75% 20-day run-up. That is mostly because RGP's company-level numbers diverge (billable hours -20.9% y/y in FQ4, management saying North America was flat sequentially). If the market expected the transmission to reach RGP's FQ2 guide, the stock would have rallied with staffing peers after the August jobs data.
findings.independence: BLS/SIA August 2026 jobs report: https://www.staffingindustry.com/research/research-reports/americas/september-2026-us-jobs-report (different source, same direction). This is a macro-to-company proxy that RGP has not confirmed; RGP's own call said conditions were 'broadly consistent to the third quarter'.

findings.finding: Consulting peers whose quarters overlap RGP's June-August quarter grew. Accenture's Q4 FY26 (June-August) consulting revenue was $9.28bn, +6%, with consulting book-to-bill of 1.0 and a FY27 guide of +3-6% local currency, and commentary that the beat eased AI-substitution fears. Korn Ferry's FQ1 FY27 (May-July) fee revenue was +7%, Workforce Solutions (interim/RPO) +11%, and remaining fees +14%. RGP's Consulting segment, about half of revenue, has cited 'longer sales cycles'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on this line. RGP did not rally with Accenture's late-September beat: its spot is below where it traded in mid-September.
findings.why_not_priced: RGP has not moved with these prints, which says the market treats RGP's decline as idiosyncratic (share loss, AI substitution of operational accounting). A sector read-through could still lift its FQ2 consulting pipeline commentary. If the market believed it, RGP would have bounced off the Accenture print.
findings.independence: Korn Ferry FQ1 FY27 release: https://www.kornferry.com/about-us/press/korn-ferry-announces-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-results-of-operations (2026-09-01), a different source in the same direction. Both are proxies; Accenture and Korn Ferry are far larger and differently mixed.

findings.finding: The FQ1 guide ($97-102m) was given 2026-07-22, about 8 of the quarter's 13 weeks in, so management had most of the quarter's billings. In the same quarter last year (FQ1 FY26, reported 2025-10-08) revenue of $120.2m, gross margin and SG&A all beat their outlook ranges. The reported quarter is therefore likely at or above the guide midpoint, inside what the company already guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2025-10-08 the stock fell -4.04% after a beat of every FQ1 FY26 outlook range. On 2026-07-22 FQ4 was an EPS beat (-$0.07 vs -$0.08) with revenue slightly below estimates, and the stock fell -18.4%. Beats on this line have been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it sits inside the company's own guide. It is filed because a small reported-quarter beat is the likely outcome, and the reaction history says it buys little.
findings.independence: The guide timing is from the FQ4 FY26 call transcript, https://www.webull.com/news/15273192387929088 (2026-07-22).

findings.finding: Simple seasonality arithmetic points slightly below the guide. Last year FQ4 to FQ1 went $139.3m to $120.2m (-13.7%); applied to FQ4 FY26's $106.1m that gives about $91.6m, under the $97m low end. Two things argue against it, which is why it is sized near zero: FQ4 FY25 probably carried an extra week (fiscal year ending 2025-05-31; not verified from a document), and the guide was set with about 8 weeks of actuals. Management's own framing was 'relatively consistent with fourth quarter levels, adjusting for normal summer seasonality and the impact of the Sitrick divestiture'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FQ4 FY26 revenue shortfall against consensus ($106.1m vs $107.8m) went with the -18.4% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference the market can make itself. It is filed small because the guide, set with intra-quarter data, overrides it.
findings.independence: Shares documents with the guide-timing finding. FQ1 FY26 revenue of $120.2m is from https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251008056558/en/Resources-Connection-Reports-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2026

baseline_tension: No skew to agree or disagree with. The mild negative lean matches the 6-of-8-down reaction history and a stock near its lows, so it is mostly priced; the peer-improvement findings cut against both and are sized small because RGP's own numbers have not followed its peers.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (a proxy loses to a company-level number): the staffing proxy (Robert Half and BLS) went from +0.6 to +0.3 and the consulting-peer proxy (Accenture and Korn Ferry) from +0.4 to +0.2, because RGP's own call said North America was flat sequentially and its billable hours were -20.9% y/y while peers stabilised.
Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the likely beat of the reported quarter went from +0.2 to +0.1, because the last FQ1 beat of every outlook range was sold (-4.04%).
Rule 6: the bar is the company guide; EPS consensus is disputed (-0.17/-0.22/-0.26), so no finding is sized on EPS. Dividend and annual-meeting items stay in outside_window.
Rule 7: short interest checked (2.45%, 2.6 days to cover), so nothing shrinks the CFO negative; it stays -1.0. p_up and abs_move unchanged (46, 9.0).
